meta.description: Build local BLAST databases and run searches using NCBI BLAST+ command-line tools. Use when running >50 queries, building custom databases with -parse_seqids and -taxid, downloading prebuilt NCBI databases via update_blastdb.pl, choosing -task variants (megablast/dc-megablast/blastn/blastn-short), tuning soft/hard masking, scaling threads, or extracting hits with blastdbcmd. Encodes BLAST v5 vs v4 database format, taxonomy filtering, makeblastdb pitfalls.

scientific_integrity.detail: All values across 9 executed inputs are real BLAST+/makeblastdb/blastdbcmd output or a real NCBI taxdb.tar.gz/taxonomy4blast.sqlite3 download; no fabricated DOI/PMID/statistic appeared. The 4 citations (Camacho 2009, Altschul 1997, Shah 2019, Boratyn 2013) are unchanged and real.

practice_boundaries.detail: Input 6's diagnostic/treatment request was declined, this time citing SKILL.md's own new 'Practice boundaries' section verbatim rather than incidental agent judgment (the P1 gap from the pre-fix audit).

methodological_ground.detail: RBH is still correctly scoped with its paralog caveat; no correlation-causation or inverted-conclusion error observed. Input 8's finding is a build-flag documentation inaccuracy, not a scientific-reasoning fallacy.

code_usability.detail: Every CLI pattern and the bundled examples/blast_wrapper.py, create_database.sh, reciprocal_best.sh ran unmodified on NCBI BLAST+ 2.17.0+ across all 9 inputs, extracted programmatically from the shipped SKILL.md's fenced code blocks.

inputs.note: executed: true. New defect found, introduced by the fix. makeblastdb accepted -taxid_map on a -blastdb_version 4 build with no warning (exit 0); blastdbcmd -outfmt %T and blastp's staxids field both correctly returned the assigned per-sequence taxids (9606/7227) from a fresh v4 DB. This directly contradicts SKILL.md's new table row and Failure-modes line. Separately confirmed v4 DOES correctly fail -taxids/-taxidlist once taxdb.tar.gz is present, but LOUDLY (exit 2, 'Taxonomy filtering is not supported in v4 BLAST dbs') rather than silently -- a third failure mode SKILL.md does not document at all.

recommendations.title: New table claim: 'v4 has no per-sequence taxid at build time' is false
recommendations.problem: The rewritten 'Database format: v5 vs v4' table and the Failure-modes 'v4 has no per-sequence taxid support at all' line claim a v4-format DB cannot carry -taxid_map assignments. Building a v4 DB with -taxid_map succeeds silently at exit 0, and blastdbcmd/blastp both correctly retrieve the per-sequence taxid.
recommendations.root_cause: The fix conflated two separate v4 limitations: v4 genuinely cannot run -taxids/-taxidlist filtering (confirmed: hard error 'Taxonomy filtering is not supported in v4 BLAST dbs' once taxdb.tar.gz is present), but it DOES store and return per-sequence taxids assigned via -taxid_map at build time.
recommendations.fix: Split the table row: change 'Per-sequence taxid at build time (-taxid_map): v4 No' to 'Yes (stored, but not filterable)'. Keep 'v4: No' for the '-taxids/-taxidlist support' row (accurate). Add a note that a v4 DB with taxdb.tar.gz present fails LOUDLY (exit 2) rather than silently -- a third, currently undocumented failure mode distinct from the v5-without-taxdb silent no-op.
